passages.text: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, pose a riddle; speak a parable to the house of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar.
passages.sermon:
The word of the LORD came to me.
God spoke to me.
God called me “son of man.”
God told me to give a riddle.
God told me to speak a parable.
God told me to speak to the house of Israel.
God told me to say, “This is what the Lord GOD says.”
A great eagle appeared.
The eagle had great wings.
The eagle had long feathers.
The eagle was full of many feathers.
The eagle’s feathers had many colors.
The eagle came to Lebanon.
The eagle took the top of the cedar tree.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם ח֥וּד חִידָ֖ה וּמְשֹׁ֣ל מָשָׁ֑ל אֶל־ בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ כֹּה־ אָמַ֣ר׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הַנֶּ֤שֶׁר הַגָּדוֹל֙ גְּד֤וֹל הַכְּנָפַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֣רֶךְ הָאֵ֔בֶר מָלֵא֙ הַנּוֹצָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ ל֖וֹ הָֽרִקְמָ֑ה בָּ֚א אֶל־ הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־ צַמֶּ֥רֶת הָאָֽרֶז׃

passages.text: He plucked off its topmost shoot, carried it to the land of merchants, and planted it in a city of traders.
passages.sermon:
A great eagle came to Lebanon.
The eagle had great wings and long pinions.
The eagle was full of feathers of many colors.
The eagle took the top of the cedar tree.
He plucked off its topmost shoot.
He carried the shoot to the land of merchants.
He planted the shoot in a city of traders.
passages.original: אֵ֛ת רֹ֥אשׁ יְנִֽיקוֹתָ֖יו קָטָ֑ף וַיְבִיאֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בְּעִ֥יר רֹכְלִ֖ים שָׂמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil; he placed it by abundant waters and set it out like a willow.
passages.sermon:
A great eagle took some seed from the land.
He planted the seed in a field of good soil.
He put the seed by much water.
He set the seed out like a willow tree.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֙ מִזֶּ֣רַע הָאָ֔רֶץ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ בִּשְׂדֵה־ זָ֑רַע קָ֚ח עַל־ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים צַפְצָפָ֖ה שָׂמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with branches turned toward him; yet its roots remained where it stood. So it became a vine and yielded branches and sent out shoots.
passages.sermon:
The plant sprouted.
It became a spreading vine.
The vine was low in height.
Its branches turned toward the one who planted it.
Its roots stayed where it was planted.
It became a vine.
It produced branches.
It sent out shoots.
passages.original: וַיִּצְמַ֡ח וַיְהִי֩ לְגֶ֨פֶן סֹרַ֜חַת שִׁפְלַ֣ת קוֹמָ֗ה לִפְנ֤וֹת דָּלִיּוֹתָיו֙ אֵלָ֔יו וְשָׁרָשָׁ֖יו תַּחְתָּ֣יו יִֽהְי֑וּ וַתְּהִ֣י לְגֶ֔פֶן וַתַּ֣עַשׂ בַּדִּ֔ים וַתְּשַׁלַּ֖ח פֹּארֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But there was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers. And behold, this vine bent its roots toward him. It stretched out its branches to him from its planting bed, so that he might water it.
passages.sermon:
There was another great eagle.
This eagle had large wings.
It had many feathers.
The vine saw this eagle.
The vine bent its roots toward the eagle.
The vine stretched out its branches to the eagle.
The vine did this from its own planting bed.
The vine wanted the eagle to water it.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י נֶֽשֶׁר־ אֶחָד֙ גָּד֔וֹל גְּד֥וֹל כְּנָפַ֖יִם וְרַב־ נוֹצָ֑ה וְהִנֵּה֩ הַגֶּ֨פֶן הַזֹּ֜את כָּֽפְנָ֧ה שָׁרֳשֶׁ֣יהָ עָלָ֗יו וְדָֽלִיּוֹתָיו֙ שִׁלְחָה־ לּ֔וֹ לְהַשְׁק֣וֹת אוֹתָ֔הּ מֵעֲרֻג֖וֹת מַטָּעָֽהּ׃

passages.text: It had been planted in good soil by abundant waters in order to yield branches and bear fruit and become a splendid vine.’
passages.sermon:
The vine was planted in good soil.
The soil was rich and healthy.
The vine was set by abundant waters.
There was plenty of water for the vine.
The purpose was for the vine to grow branches.
The purpose was for the vine to bear fruit.
The purpose was for the vine to become a splendid vine.
passages.original: אֶל־ שָׂ֥דֶה טּ֛וֹב אֶל־ מַ֥יִם רַבִּ֖ים הִ֣יא שְׁתוּלָ֑ה לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עָנָף֙ וְלָשֵׂ֣את פֶּ֔רִי לִהְי֖וֹת לְגֶ֥פֶן אַדָּֽרֶת׃ס

passages.text: So you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Will it flourish? Will it not be uprooted and stripped of its fruit so that it shrivels? All its foliage will wither! It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He asks a question about the vine.
He says, "Will this vine flourish?"
He says, "No, it will not flourish."
He says, "Someone will uproot its roots."
He says, "Someone will strip away its fruit."
The vine will shrivel.
All its leaves will wither.
No one will need a strong arm to do this.
No large group of people will be needed to pull it up by its roots.
passages.original: אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִ֖ה תִּצְלָ֑ח הֲלוֹא֩ אֶת־ שָׁרָשֶׁ֨יהָ יְנַתֵּ֜ק וְאֶת־ פִּרְיָ֣הּ׀ יְקוֹסֵ֣ס וְיָבֵ֗שׁ כָּל־ טַרְפֵּ֤י צִמְחָהּ֙ תִּיבָ֔שׁ וְלֹֽא־ בִזְרֹ֤עַ גְּדוֹלָה֙ וּבְעַם־ רָ֔ב לְמַשְׂא֥וֹת אוֹתָ֖הּ מִשָּׁרָשֶֽׁיהָ׃

passages.text: Even if it is transplanted, will it flourish? Will it not completely wither when the east wind strikes? It will wither on the bed where it sprouted.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God speaks about a vine.
The vine was planted in good soil.
The vine had plenty of water.
The vine was meant to grow strong.
The vine was meant to bear fruit.
The vine was meant to become splendid.
God asks a question about the vine.
He says, “Even if the vine is transplanted, will it flourish?”
He asks, “Will it not wither when the east wind strikes it?”
God says the vine will wither.
It will dry up on the bed where it was planted.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׁתוּלָ֖ה הֲתִצְלָ֑ח הֲלוֹא֩ כְגַ֨עַת בָּ֜הּ ר֤וּחַ הַקָּדִים֙ תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ עַל־ עֲרֻגֹ֥ת צִמְחָ֖הּ תִּיבָֽשׁ׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Now say to this rebellious house: ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them, ‘Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, carried off its king and officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a message.
He told me to speak to the people of Israel.
These people are rebellious.
God called them the rebellious house.
God asked them a question.
He said, “Do you not know what these things mean?”
God told me what to say to them.
He said, “Look at what happened.”
The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem.
He took the king of Jerusalem.
He took the officials of Jerusalem.
He brought the king and the officials to Babylon.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֱמָר־ נָא֙ לְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔רִי הֲלֹ֥א יְדַעְתֶּ֖ם מָה־ אֵ֑לֶּה אֱמֹ֗ר הִנֵּה־ בָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֤ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־ מַלְכָּהּ֙ וְאֶת־ שָׂרֶ֔יהָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אוֹתָ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: He took a member of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. Then he carried away the leading men of the land, so that the kingdom would be brought low, unable to lift itself up, surviving only by keeping his covenant.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem.
He took a member of the royal family.
He made a covenant with this royal family member.
He put him under oath.
He also took away the leading men of the land.
He did this so the kingdom would become low and weak.
The kingdom could not lift itself up.
The kingdom could survive only by keeping the king of Babylon’s covenant.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֙ מִזֶּ֣רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת אִתּ֖וֹ בְּרִ֑ית וַיָּבֵ֤א אֹתוֹ֙ בְּאָלָ֔ה וְאֶת־ אֵילֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לָקָֽח׃ לִֽהְיוֹת֙ מַמְלָכָ֣ה שְׁפָלָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֖י הִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א לִשְׁמֹ֥ר אֶת־ בְּרִית֖וֹ לְעָמְדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: But this king rebelled against Babylon by sending his envoys to Egypt to ask for horses and a large army. Will he flourish? Will the one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and yet escape?’
passages.sermon:
The king of Judah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
He sent his messengers to Egypt.
He asked Egypt for horses.
He asked Egypt for a large army.
Will this king succeed?
Will a person who does these things escape?
Can someone break a covenant and still escape?
passages.original: וַיִּמְרָד־ בּ֗וֹ לִשְׁלֹ֤חַ מַלְאָכָיו֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָֽתֶת־ ל֥וֹ סוּסִ֖ים וְעַם־ רָ֑ב הֲיִצְלָ֤ח הֲיִמָּלֵט֙ הָעֹשֵׂ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וְהֵפֵ֥ר בְּרִ֖ית וְנִמְלָֽט׃

passages.text: ‘As surely as I live,’ declares the Lord GOD, ‘he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who enthroned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD says, "As surely as I live."
A king placed this man on the throne.
This man despised the king's oath.
This man broke the king's covenant.
This man will die in Babylon.
He will die in the land of the king who made him king.
passages.original: חַי־ אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ אִם־ לֹ֗א בִּמְקוֹם֙ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַמַּמְלִ֣יךְ אֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּזָה֙ אֶת־ אָ֣לָת֔וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵפֵ֖ר אֶת־ בְּרִית֑וֹ אִתּ֥וֹ בְתוֹךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are built and siege walls constructed to destroy many lives.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh has a mighty army.
Pharaoh has a vast horde of people.
Pharaoh will not help him in battle.
People will build ramps for attack.
People will construct siege walls.
These things will happen to destroy many lives.
passages.original: וְלֹא֩ בְחַ֨יִל גָּד֜וֹל וּבְקָהָ֣ל רָ֗ב יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה אוֹת֤וֹ פַרְעֹה֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בִּשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ סֹלְלָ֖ה וּבִבְנ֣וֹת דָּיֵ֑ק לְהַכְרִ֖ית נְפָשׁ֥וֹת רַבּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Seeing that he gave his hand in pledge yet did all these things, he will not escape!’
passages.sermon:
The king broke his covenant.
He despised the oath.
He gave his hand in pledge.
He did all these things.
He will not escape.
passages.original: וּבָזָ֥ה אָלָ֖ה לְהָפֵ֣ר בְּרִ֑ית וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֥ן יָד֛וֹ וְכָל־ אֵ֥לֶּה עָשָׂ֖ה לֹ֥א יִמָּלֵֽט׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘As surely as I live, I will bring down upon his head My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He is the one true God.
He lives forever.
He makes a promise.
He says, “As surely as I live, I will act.”
He refers to the man who despised His oath.
This man broke God’s covenant.
God will punish this man.
God will bring His oath down on this man’s head.
God will bring His broken covenant down on this man’s head.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־ אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֮ חַי־ אָנִי֒ אִם־ לֹ֗א אָֽלָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּזָ֔ה וּבְרִיתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵפִ֑יר וּנְתַתִּ֖יו בְּרֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: I will spread My net over him and catch him in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon and execute judgment upon him there for the treason he committed against Me.
passages.sermon:
God is the speaker.
God acts with authority and power.
God says, "I will spread My net over him."
I will catch him in My snare.
I will bring him to Babylon.
I will judge him there.
He committed treason against Me.
I will execute judgment for his treason.
passages.original: וּפָרַשְׂתִּ֤י עָלָיו֙ רִשְׁתִּ֔י וְנִתְפַּ֖שׂ בִּמְצֽוּדָתִ֑י וַהֲבִיאוֹתִ֣יהוּ בָבֶ֗לָה וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּ֤י אִתּוֹ֙ שָׁ֔ם מַעֲל֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָֽעַל־ בִּֽי׃

passages.text: All his choice troops will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.’
passages.sermon:
The Lord is speaking.
The Lord is powerful and judges justly.
All his best soldiers will die by the sword.
Anyone who survives will scatter in every direction.
You will know that I am the Lord.
You will know that I have spoken.
passages.original: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ מִבְרָחוֹ בְּכָל־ אֲגַפָּיו֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִ֖ים לְכָל־ ר֣וּחַ יִפָּרֵ֑שׂוּ וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃ס

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD has all power and authority.
The Lord GOD says what will happen.
The Lord GOD will act.
The Lord GOD will take a shoot.
This shoot comes from the top of a tall cedar tree.
The Lord GOD will set out this shoot.
The Lord GOD will pick a tender sprig.
This sprig comes from the highest branches of the cedar.
The Lord GOD will plant this sprig.
The Lord GOD will plant it on a high mountain.
The mountain will be tall and lofty.
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְלָקַ֣חְתִּי אָ֗נִי מִצַּמֶּ֧רֶת הָאֶ֛רֶז הָרָמָ֖ה וְנָתָ֑תִּי מֵרֹ֤אשׁ יֹֽנְקוֹתָיו֙ רַ֣ךְ אֶקְטֹ֔ף וְשָׁתַ֣לְתִּי אָ֔נִי עַ֥ל הַר־ גָּבֹ֖הַ וְתָלֽוּל׃

passages.text: I will plant it on the mountain heights of Israel so that it will bear branches; it will yield fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it, taking shelter in the shade of its branches.
passages.sermon:
The Lord God is speaking.
He will plant a tender shoot on the high mountain of Israel.
This shoot will grow strong.
It will send out branches.
It will produce fruit.
It will become a great and majestic cedar tree.
Every kind of bird will come to it.
All birds will find a home under its branches.
They will rest in the shade of its limbs.
passages.original: בְּהַ֨ר מְר֤וֹם יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶשְׁתֳּלֶ֔נּוּ וְנָשָׂ֤א עָנָף֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה פֶ֔רִי וְהָיָ֖ה לְאֶ֣רֶז אַדִּ֑יר וְשָׁכְנ֣וּ תַחְתָּ֗יו כֹּ֚ל צִפּ֣וֹר כָּל־ כָּנָ֔ף בְּצֵ֥ל דָּלִיּוֹתָ֖יו תִּשְׁכֹּֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD. I bring the tall tree down and make the low tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
He acts with power and authority.
All the trees of the field will know Him.
He brings down the tall tree.
He makes the low tree tall.
He dries up the green tree.
He makes the withered tree flourish.
The LORD has spoken.
The LORD has done it.
passages.original: וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל־ עֲצֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ הִשְׁפַּ֣לְתִּי׀ עֵ֣ץ גָּבֹ֗הַ הִגְבַּ֙הְתִּי֙ עֵ֣ץ שָׁפָ֔ל הוֹבַ֙שְׁתִּי֙ עֵ֣ץ לָ֔ח וְהִפְרַ֖חְתִּי עֵ֣ץ יָבֵ֑שׁ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִֽׂיתִי׃פ
